highlights.title: Watch: Log Carbs fallback when bolus is zero
changes: If the recommended bolus is zero, the watch shows a "No Bolus, Log Carbs" button so you can log carbs without a bolus.
Turning the insulin dial above zero restores the "Enact Bolus" button and opens the bolus confirmation flow.
Tapping the "No Bolus, Log Carbs" button logs the carbs from the watch and shows an acknowledgment screen.
The watch shows a "Calculating Bolus..." progress state while waiting for the phone and clears it on reply, error, or a.
The insulin amount is snapped to the configured increment so tiny dial residues do not count as a non-zero bolus.

highlights.title: Fix forecast lines not drawing in chart
changes: Forecast lines in the main chart now render as connected lines instead of collapsing to points.
This fixes cases where forecast series could disappear on some builds.
The forecast cone and Live Activity visuals are unchanged by this fix.

changes: Opening Nightscout configuration from the Home CGM sheet no longer crashes the app.
The Nightscout 'Fetch' and 'Upload' screens now open correctly from that Home sheet.
Settings search highlight behavior is preserved when accessing Nightscout from Home.

includedPullRequests.title: Add watch "Log Carbs" fallback when recommended bolus is zero
includedPullRequests.body:
In the watch "Meal & Bolus" flow, the bolus screen's only action was "Enact Bolus", disabled whenever the amount was 0 U. A 0 U recommendation is a normal outcome (low glucose, stale loop, or IOB already covering the meal), so the user hit a dead end: back out to the root, choose "Meal", and re-enter the carbs.

Now, when carbs were carried in from the combo flow and the insulin dial sits at zero, the button becomes "Log Carbs" and logs the carbs directly (matching the standalone "Meal" path). Dialing insulin above zero flips it back to "Enact Bolus" and the existing crown-confirm path is unchanged. The zero check is taken against the increment-snapped amount so floating-point residue from dialing the crown up and back down does not read as a non-zero bolus.

To keep a fast tap from logging carbs before the phone's recommendation arrives, requestBolusRecommendation() now drives the existing (previously unused) "Calculating Bolus..." progress state, cleared on reply, on send error, or after a 3s timeout.

Demo video on simulator: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/o-QPaloI03A

includedPullRequests.title: Use unique ids to draw forecast lines
includedPullRequests.body:
### Problem

`ForecastView.drawForecastsLines()` keyed its `ForEach` on `\.id`:

```swift
ForEach(preprocessedData, id: \.id) { tuple in
```

That id isn't unique per row. `fetchForecastHierarchy` mints one `UUID()` per
*forecast*, and `ForecastSetup` stamps it onto every value in that forecast — so
~240 rows share ~5 identities. Duplicate ids in a `ForEach` are undefined
behaviour; SwiftUI may collapse them, leaving each series a single point and a
`LineMark` nothing to connect.

The cone is unaffected (`ForEach(0 ..< n, id: \.self)`), as is the Live Activity,
which uses the same unique-index pattern.

### Fix

```swift
ForEach(preprocessedData, id: \.forecastValue.objectID) { tuple in
```

Every row is a distinct `ForecastValue` managed object, so its `objectID` is
unique by construction and stable across fetches — no allocation, no positional
identity. Series grouping comes from `foregroundStyle(by:)`, not `ForEach`
identity, so lines neither merge nor split.

### Why it needs a fix

It seems we've just been lucky until now, but building with Xcode 27 causes the forecast lines to not display at all in the main chart because of this.

includedPullRequests.title: Fix crash in HomeRootView by injecting the existing SettingsSearchHighlight instance
includedPullRequests.body:
`NightscoutUploadView` and `NightscoutFetchView` require a `SettingsSearchHighlight` environment object that is missing when Nightscout configuration is opened from the Home-screen CGM sheet.

Cause of the crash is https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/commit/5cb78b6af0bae7751167527160d7f9232a9559b2 which added `.settingsHighlightScroll()` to these two views.

- Both destinations apply `.settingsHighlightScroll()`
- That modifier unconditionally reads  `@Environment(SettingsSearchHighlight.self)`
- The object is injected only into the Settings tab’s `NavigationStack`
- The Home-screen CGM sheet is outside that subtree, so navigating to Upload or Fetch causes SwiftUI’s fatal “no observable object of type `SettingsSearchHighlight` found” failure
- Settings to Services to Nightscout works because that route inherits the required environment object

So we can inject the existing settings-highlight environment into the Home CGM sheet so the Nightscout child routes inherit it, without changing the working `Settings` navigation path.

PR fixes the crash in `HomeRootView.swift` by injecting the existing `SettingsSearchHighlight` instance into the Home-screen CGM configuration sheet. Nightscout’s Upload and Fetch views now inherit their required environment dependency.

Fixes #1480 

**Test steps:**
1. Enable nightscout as a CGM (you may need to delete your existing CGM and set up nightscout as the CGM)
2. Click on your CGM and configure nightscout, then go to 'Fetch' or 'Upload' and verify the subscreens open without crashing
